title: William Hauptman
source:
{{short description|American dramatist}} '''William Hauptman''' (born 1942) is an American writer. Born in Texas, he received a BFA from the [[University of Texas]] Drama Department and later traveled to San Francisco and New York. A graduate who received an MFA from the [[Yale School of Drama]],{{cite web|url=https://www.rnh.com/bio/207/Hauptman-William |title=William Hauptman :: Rodgers & Hammerstein :: Bio Details |publisher=Rnh.com |access-date=2018-09-13}} he is the author of plays and fiction. == Career == His various plays include: ''Shearwater'' ([[American Place Theater]]) (1974) ''Heat'' ([[The Public Theater]]){{cite web|last=Albee |first=Edward |url=https://www.samuelfrench.com/p/3918/heat |title=Heat |publisher=Samuel French |access-date=2018-09-13}} (1974) And ''Domino Courts and Comanche Cafe'' (1976) at the [[American Place Theatre]] which won a Village Voice [[Obie Award]] (1977).{{cite web|url=http://www.brooklyneagle.com/articles/2018/4/17/brooklyn-author-uses-life-experience-pen-new-book-about-westward-journey-%E2%80%9960s |title=Brooklyn author uses life experience to pen new book about a westward journey in the '60s | Brooklyn Daily Eagle |publisher=Brooklyneagle.com |date=2018-04-17 |access-date=2018-09-13}} ''[[Big River (musical)|Big River]]'' (1985), his adaptation of [[Mark Twain]]'s ''[[Huckleberry Finn]]'', written in collaboration with composer [[Roger Miller]],{{cite web|last=Simon |first=John |url=https://nymag.com/nymetro/arts/theater/reviews/n_9051/ |title=Big River, Avenue Q - New York Magazine Theater Review |publisher=Nymag.com |date=2015-07-22 |access-date=2018-09-13}} won seven Tony Awards, including Best Musical and Best Book of a Musical when it opened on [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]]. It has proven very popular in stock and amateur theatrical productions.{{cite web|title=Big River|url=http://www.playbillvault.com/Show/Detail/4707/Big-River#Awards|website=Playbill Vault|access-date=31 July 2015|ref=Playbill Vault}} Hauptman joined the project after being approached by former [[Yale University|Yale]] classmate [[Rocco Landesman]]. Hauptman is also a writer of fiction. His first published story, ''Good Rockin' Tonight'', about an [[Elvis]] impersonator, made The Best American Short Stories Collection of 1982.{{cite web|url=https://www.goodreads.com/author/list/451196.William_Hauptman |title=Books by William Hauptman (Author of Storm Season) |publisher=Goodreads.com |access-date=2018-09-13}} Later, Hauptman wrote a screenplay of this story for [[20th Century Fox]], going on to write several other screenplays for the studios, including [[Amblin Entertainment]] and [[Merchant Ivory Productions]]. Bantam published his collection of short stories, including ''Good Rockin' Tonight and Other Stories'' (1988). [[Larry McMurtry]] gave him this quote: "William Hauptman, for my money, is the most promising young fiction writers to come out of the Southwest in a long time."{{cite web|url=http://williamhauptman.net/WH_fiction.html |title=William Hauptman, fiction |publisher=Williamhauptman.net |access-date=2018-09-13}} This collection won the Jesse Jones Award for Best Work of Fiction given by the Texas Institute of Letters in 1989, along with an award for Best Short Story, which was given to ''Moon Walking''.{{Cite web |title=TIL Members Complete History |url=http://www.texasinstituteofletters.org/archives/TIL-members-complete-history.pdf |website=www.texasinstituteofletters.org}} In 1992, Bantam published his novel about tornado-chasers ''The Storm Season'', which was later reprinted by the University of Texas Press. This novel was praised by [[Carolyn See]] in the [[Los Angeles Times]], who said, "Storm Season is about family, the working class, the crimes human beings have committed against the land, and the hypnotic, redemptive quality of disaster--why human beings enjoy being scared out of their wits. It's spooky, beautiful, bizarre."{{cite web|author=Carolyn See |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-03-09-vw-2446-story.html |title='Storm Season': Wild, Original and Gorgeous : THE STORM SEASON, by William Hauptman, Bantam Books, $19.50, 306 pages - latimes |publisher=Articles.latimes.com |date=1992-03-09 |access-date=2018-09-13}} His most recent novel, about his experiences in the 60s, is called ''Journey to the West'' (2017) which has been described by James Magnuson, director of the Michener Center at the University of Texas as "by turns hilarious, sweet, and harrowing...It deserves to be a classic."{{cite web|url=http://www.journeytothewestbook.com |title=Journey to the West by William Hauptman |publisher=Journeytothewestbook.com |access-date=2018-09-13}} [[Big River (musical)|Big River]] was also produced by the Deaf West Company in both Los Angeles (2002) and New York, (2003) at the [[American Airlines Theater]], and received a [[Tony Award for Best Revival of a Musical]].{{cite web|url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/tonyawardsshowinfo.php?showname=Big%20River |title=Big River Tony Awards Info |publisher=Broadwayworld.com |access-date=2018-09-13}} Big River was also produced as part of the Encores Series at City Center Theater in New York in 2017. Program Notes: From Playbill of Encores Production of Big River, 2016: "It was a time when everybody played by the rules of Satchel Paige: Don't worry about the things you can't do nothing about, dance like nobody's watching, and love like you can't get hurt." He has also contributed articles to [[The Atlantic Monthly]], Texas Monthly, and [[The New York Times]] Sunday Magazine.{{cite news|last=Hauptman |first=William |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/08/07/magazine/will-the-world-flock-to-wichita-falls.html |title=Will The World Flock To Wichita Falls? - The New York Times |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=7 August 1988 |access-date=2018-09-13}} Teaching Experience—Yale School of Drama; the Michener Center for writers at the University of Texas in Austin; and [[Brooklyn College]]. *''[[Big River (musical)|Big River]]'' *''Heat''{{cite web|author=William Hauptman |url=https://www.samuelfrench.com/s/3918/heat |title=Heat |publisher=Samuel French |access-date=2018-09-13}} *''Comanche Cafe'' *''Domino Courts''{{cite web|author=William Hauptman |url=https://www.samuelfrench.com/s/5712/comanche-cafe |title=Comanche Cafe |publisher=Samuel French |access-date=2018-09-13}} *''Gillette''{{cite web|author=William Hauptman |url=https://www.samuelfrench.com/s/5643/gillette |title=Gillette |publisher=Samuel French |access-date=2018-09-13}} *''Good Rockin' Tonight and Other Stories'' *''The Storm Season'' *Journey to the West == Awards == * 1979 [[NAACP]] Freedom Foundation Award - [[PBS]] teleplay [[Denmark Vesey]], starring [[Ned Beatty]] and [[Yaphet Kotto]], - '''Winner'''{{cite web|last=Shepard |first=Richard F. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1982/02/17/arts/tv-a-forgotton-rebellion-of-slaves.html |title=Tv: A Forgotten Rebellion Of Slaves - The New York Times |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=1982-02-17 |access-date=2018-09-13}} * 1985 *[[Tony Award for Best Musical]] - ''[[Big River (musical)|Big River]]'' - '''Winner''' * 1986 Los Angeles Drama Critics Circle Award for Best Play, ''Gillette'' - '''Winner''' * 1988 Jesse Jones Award for Best Book from the Texas Institute of Letters for ''Good Rockin' Tonight'' -- '''Winner''' * 2003 *[[Tony Award for Best Revival of a Musical]] by the Deaf West Company of Los Angeles, ''[[Big River (musical)|Big River]]'', at the [[American Airlines Theatre]] in New York. - '''Winner''' * '''Grants''': National Endowment Grant, Rockefeller Grant, Guggenheim Grant
'''Honors''': The Author has also been included in the exclusive Texas Writer's Collection at Texas State University.{{cite web|url=http://www.thewittliffcollections.txstate.edu/research/a-z/hauptman.html |title=William Hauptman : The Wittliff Collections |publisher=Thewittliffcollections.txstate.edu |date=1942-11-26 |access-date=2018-09-13}} == Personal life == Hauptman is married to Marjorie Erdreich and lives in Brooklyn. His daughter, Sarah, is employed by the State Department and their son, Max, is a captain in the United States Army.{{cite web|url=http://williamhauptman.net/WH_about.html |title=About William Hauptman |publisher=Williamhauptman.net |access-date=2018-09-13}} "I live in Brooklyn because, for all its faults, I like it better than the town where I was born. My days are calm and predetermined. I watch my children grow up and hope they will do well." -''Journey to the West''{{cite book|last=Hauptman |first=William |title=Journey to the West |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Py87DwAAQBAJ |date=8 September 2017 |publisher=iUniverse |isbn=978-1-5320-2235-7}} ==References== {{reflist}} == External links == *{{IMDb name|id=1105330|name=William Hauptman}} {{TonyAward MusicalBook 1976–2000}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Hauptman, William}} [[Category:20th-century American dramatists and playwrights]] [[Category:American short story writers]] [[Category:Tony Award winners]] [[Category:1942 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Wichita Falls, Texas]] [[Category:Brooklyn College faculty]]
